command: Human RGR P47804 enables G-protein-coupled receptor/photoreceptor activity, participates in GPCR signaling and phototransduction, and is active in the plasma membrane. Evaluate each separately using full primary studies, exact GO definitions and isoform context. Exact target PTN002517412 descends from opsin ancestral IBD PTN008398221 for all five propagated terms; assess inheritance or target divergence, not donor counts. PMID18474598 directly shows light-dependent regulation of retinyl-ester mobilization in human RPE/mouse models and explicitly leaves open a G-protein or another signaling mechanism. Its GRY/NAXXY motifs are not a direct negative G-protein assay; identify any positive or appropriately controlled negative coupling assays, including non-ocular contexts such as PMID linked to PMC9014095. Photoisomerase function does not itself disprove a second signaling capacity. GO0007602 is conversion of absorbed photons into a molecular signal and does not explicitly demand heterotrimeric G protein, so distinguish its scope from GO0008020/0004930, which require GDP/GTP exchange on a G-protein alpha subunit. Evaluate light-regulated enzyme activity and chromophore production against that distinction. PMID27011730 full text directly localizes exon6-skipping RGR-d to human RPE basolateral plasma membrane with splice-specific DE21 antibody and controls. Normal RGR is ER-associated. This resolves simple gene-level location but not necessarily the IBA qualifier is_active_in or whether a human-specific splice variant establishes the ancestral assertion. Do not use ER localization as proof of no plasma-membrane isoform; determine whether functional activity at that membrane is established. PMID7947717 retinal binding is bovine RGR plus human sequence, not all direct human experiments. Separate primary biochemical evidence from a historical GPCR name or propagated database assertions.
